title: Orchestrated SLO policy engine for VPC probe fleet and Terraform rollout
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a configurable orchestration layer and accompanying Terraform module to deploy, calibrate, and roll out SLO probe policies across private (VPC) deployments. The system should manage synthetic + passive probes for latency, error-rate, saturation, and token-throughput, support canaries and phased rollouts, and provide a safe upgrade path and runbook for operators.

Motivation: Current VPC probe configurations are fragmented: different stacks have divergent thresholds, sampling rates, and alerting rules. Upgrades to the private control plane or runtime have required manual probe tuning, causing noisy alerts or missed regressions. We need a single, reproducible IaC surface that: (1) describes probe topology and thresholds, (2) provides calibration jobs to compute baselines for each VPC cluster group, (3) supports canary-aware adjustments, and (4) integrates with our dashboards and runbooks for incident response.

Requirements: 
- Probe types: synthetic (endpoint-level p95/p99 latency, end-to-end success rate), passive (service error rate, 5xx rates), saturation (GPU queue length, OOM events), token throughput (tokens/sec per worker and aggregate per VPC).
- Config model: hierarchical policy: global defaults -> org/tenant overrides -> cluster-group overrides -> instance overrides. Policies expressed as versioned JSON/YAML documents managed via Terraform state (SSM param store or remote state module).
- Calibration: a daily calibration job that computes rolling baselines and produces suggested thresholds (e.g., p95 baseline * 1.35 for alerting). Calibration results must be auditable and retained for 90 days.
- Canary awareness: when rolling runtime or model upgrades (private-rolling-upgrades), probes should run denser sampling against canary subset and automatically suppress noisy alerts for the canary window or route alerts to a separate on-call.
- Observability: probe outputs must feed into Prometheus/Cortex with labels (vpc_id, cluster_group, probe_version, canary_tags). Dashboards per VPC and cluster group with token throughput heatmaps.
- Alerting: Mute/auto-escalation policies, runbook links, automated rollback trigger if token throughput drops >40% for 5m combined with increased p99 latency >2x baseline.
- IaC: A Terraform module that deploys: probe configs (SSM or configmap depending on private vs on-prem), cron calibration job (k8s CronJob or ECS scheduled task), Prometheus scrape jobs, and RBAC for probes to access metrics. Module must be backwards-compatible with existing probe exporters.
- Testing: e2e integration tests in staging that run synthetic load and assert probe detection and alert lifecycle.

Design notes / trade-offs: 
- We will avoid building a custom metrics store; use Prometheus + Cortex (existing infra) and an intermediate translation layer that converts probe outputs into metrics. This reduces operational burden but adds label cardinality considerations.
- Baseline-based thresholds are adaptive but risk masking regressions during slow degradation; mitigation: maintain a fixed "alerting floor" and use regression detectors in Optimize.
- Calibration frequency: daily by default; allow per-VPC override. More frequent calibrations increase noise and CPU usage.

Deliverables: 
- Terraform module: sources/infra/modules/vpc-probes (inputs, outputs, examples)
- Kubernetes manifests or ECS task definitions for calibration job
- Probe orchestration service (small controller) that applies policies to the probe fleet and coordinates canary phases (stateless controller implemented as Go service, image pushed to private registry)
- Runbook and playbook with rollback automation hooks
- Dashboards and alert rules: grafana/dashboard-json and alertmanager rules checked into infra repo

Success criteria: 
- All new VPCs provisioned by the module have a consistent probe configuration and calibration job enabled by default.
- In staging, an induced 30% token throughput regression is detected by probes and triggers an automated canary escalation path (quiet alert then page if persists).
- Upgrade rollout docs show at least one real production rollout using the module without unplanned pager noise in the first 72h.

Migration path: 
1) Land Terraform module behind feature flag for new VPCs.
2) Run calibration job in read-only mode for existing VPCs to collect baselines.
3) Adopt policies for a single pilot customer VPC and monitor for 1 week.
4) Gradual conversion of other VPCs with automated PR generation that updates infra repositories.

Safety and rollback: include automatic suppression of noisy alerts during planned upgrades, an opt-out flag per-VPC, and a preflight check that verifies calibration data exists before enabling auto-escalation.

Notes: this ticket focuses on the orchestration + IaC surface. Separate follow-ups will harden probe exporters and storage retention policies.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Chen: Initial proposal drafted after on-call postmortem. Added requirements and migration plan. Seeking feedback from infra and runtime teams.

2025-02-14 - Diego Morales: Reviewed and added canary-awareness details. Suggest adding a 'probe-version' label to make rollbacks easier. Will prototype the controller in a sidecar first before a dedicated service.

2025-02-20 - Lila Patel (SRE): Concern: Prometheus label cardinality with per-vpc baselines. Suggest storing baselines in SSM and only emitting aggregate metrics; calibration job should write suggested thresholds back to SSM instead of adding labels to metrics.
Action: SRE to run a cardinality impact assessment for 10 pilot VPCs.

2025-02-25 - Diego Morales: Terraform module skeleton PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1187. Contains module inputs, examples, and initial RBAC. Marked 'do not merge' until calibration job and controller prototype land.

2025-02-28 - QA: Ran staging calibration job against staging-vpc-3. Results: p95 baseline computed, suggested thresholds saved to SSM. Synthetic probe detected injected 40% token throughput drop and created an alert but was muted for 5m per canary policy. Need to tighten mute logic to account for parallel degradations.
Follow-up: adjust mute window to 3m for short blips and rely on aggregation across 3 consecutive windows for escalation.

2025-03-04 - Diego Morales: Controller prototype (sidecar-mode) validated in dev cluster. Next: convert to controller binary, add Terraform module integration tests, and schedule PR for infra with unit/integration tests. Blocking: SRE cardinality assessment (expected by 2025-03-07).
